name: Easing
summary: Standard smoothing for the moment you start moving from a standstill.

where.text: Edit your Config (pencil icon). In Mouse Aim or Motion Aim, set Smoothing to Custom instead of a preset, and make sure the smoothing button reads STANDARD (press it to change modes). Easing is one of the Standard settings.

citations.quote: To edit the current Config, press the pencil icon.
Here you can set Sensitivity (remember that lower values are faster) and Smoothing.
Motion aim settings consists of Sensitivity and Smoothing.
You can also customize the smoothing system and choose between two smoothing modes: Standard and Classic.
It's recommended you use one of the smoothing presets. If you are using "custom", ensure you do not reduce smoothing intensity below that of the presets.
Press the the smoothing button (i.e. "STANDARD" or "CLASSIC") to change modes.
Easing Specifies aim behavior from rest

definition.text: Specifies aim behavior from rest. Higher values result in smoother transition from rest but lower response time.

citations.quote: Higher values result in smoother transition from rest but lower response time.

definition.caveat: The official wording is ambiguous: we read 'lower response time' as less responsive because of the 'but'. Confirm in-game before relying on it.

plainWords.text: It sets how your aim behaves as it starts moving from rest.
Higher Easing should make that start smoother but less responsive. Lower Easing should give a quicker, less smoothed start.

citations.quote: Higher values result in smoother transition from rest but lower response time.

plainWords.reasoning: The definition pairs "smoother transition from rest" with "but lower response time". The "but" marks a cost, so we read "lower response time" as less responsive.
plainWords.caveat: The official wording is ambiguous: we read 'lower response time' as less responsive because of the 'but'. Confirm in-game before relying on it.

plainWords.text: The guide doesn't give this setting's range or default. Check what Manager shows before you change it.

feel.text: Higher Easing gives a smoother transition from rest.

citations.quote: Higher values result in smoother transition from rest but lower response time.

feel.caveat: The official wording is ambiguous: we read 'lower response time' as less responsive because of the 'but'. Confirm in-game before relying on it.

guidance.text: The guide gives no recommended value for this setting. It says smoothing is "strictly based on preference" and suggests trying the presets first.

citations.quote: Both mouse and motion have different presets designed for those aiming methods. Start by trying each out to see what feels most natural to you. It's strictly based on preference.

aimStyles.text: Snap: the main lever. Peeks and snaps start from a standstill. Lower Easing should give a faster start, at the cost of a less smooth one. Higher Easing should give a smoother but slower start.

citations.quote: Higher values result in smoother transition from rest but lower response time.

aimStyles.reasoning: Easing "Specifies aim behavior from rest", and a snap begins at rest. The direction comes from our reading of "smoother transition from rest but lower response time".
aimStyles.caveat: The official wording is ambiguous: we read 'lower response time' as less responsive because of the 'but'. Confirm in-game before relying on it.

aimStyles.text: Precision hold: can matter. A careful line-up often starts from a standstill, and higher Easing should make that start smoother.

citations.quote: Higher values result in smoother transition from rest but lower response time.

aimStyles.reasoning: Easing acts on the start from rest, and higher values give a "smoother transition from rest".
aimStyles.caveat: The official wording is ambiguous: we read 'lower response time' as less responsive because of the 'but'. Confirm in-game before relying on it.

aimStyles.text: Tracking: matters less. While you track, the reticle is rarely at rest, so Easing only acts as the track begins.
aimStyles.reasoning: Easing is defined only for aim "from rest".

confusions.name: Stability
confusions.note: Stability is about aim at rest (holding still, motion aim only). Easing is about the start of movement from rest.

confusions.name: Response
confusions.note: The "response time" in Easing's definition is not the Response setting, which controls fast aim.

confusions.name: Smooth ADS Transition
confusions.note: Blends the switch from Hip to ADS aim. It is an ADS option, not Easing's "transition from rest".
